solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Harbours attracting sailor in standard bit of garb

indicators.note: the harbours and sailor sit inside the word for standard, which opens to hold them

parts.note: set, as in a set or standard pattern

indicators.note: the harbours draw the sailor in beside them, so the two pieces join

parts.note: ports are harbours
Jack, as in Jack Tar, is a sailor

explanation.surface: Ports full of sailors are dressed in some standard item of clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Standard' as a noun suggests a flag, but here it is SET, as in a set or fixed norm.
explanation.definitionFit: A tweed jacket worn casually is one item of clothing, so it is a bit of garb.

clue.text: Fool that is not heartless or wise

parts.note: a sap is a gullible fool
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

indicators.note: the middle of the word not is removed, leaving its outside letters

explanation.surface: A puzzle over whether a fool is unfeeling or wise.
explanation.definitionFit: A direct synonym: someone sapient has wisdom and discernment.

clue.text: Some coloratura reportedly uplifting in this

definitions.text: Some coloratura reportedly uplifting in this

indicators.note: in a down clue lifting up means the run is read from bottom to top
only some letters of the words that follow are taken, a run spanning both

explanation.surface: Reports say some showy coloratura singing is uplifting in this kind of work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes RAREPO from coloratuRA REPOrtedly, and 'uplifting' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Coloratura singing, ornate soprano runs, is found in stage works sung throughout, which is what this whole clue describes.

clue.text: First-rate way to reach the attic?

definitions.meaning: the uppermost set of stairs in a house leads up to the loft

explanation.definitionFit: Top-flight means of the highest quality, and literally the highest staircase leads up to the loft.

clue.text: Judge copy to be some sort of prank

parts.note: to ape is to imitate or copy

explanation.surface: A judge's imitation turns out to be some kind of practical joke.
explanation.definitionFit: A jape is a playful trick or joke, the same thing as a prank.

clue.text: Pen capturing revolutionary operation of the body

indicators.note: the enclosure word holds the other piece inside it, as a captive

parts.note: a corral is a pen for livestock

indicators.note: turning round, so the abbreviation is read backwards

explanation.surface: A writing pen gets hold of a revolutionary bodily operation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pen' is the livestock enclosure, not a writing tool.
explanation.definitionFit: Corporal as an adjective means relating to the body, as in corporal punishment.

clue.text: Follow aim to exclude finale — it's omitted from set of pieces

indicators.note: the last letter of the word for aim is dropped

parts.note: an end is an aim or goal

indicators.note: the letters of it are left out of the word for a set of pieces

parts.note: a suite is a set of musical pieces, or of furniture
it's here means it is, so the word it is what goes

explanation.surface: Instructions for a musical programme: pursue a goal but drop the finale from the suite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to exclude finale' makes EN from END; 'omitted from' makes SUE from SUITE.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensue is to follow on afterwards, as a result or in sequence.

clue.text: Easy work to go wrong over energy treatment?

indicators.note: in a down answer the first piece sits over, above, the rest

parts.note: to sin is to do wrong
E is the physics symbol for energy
a cure is a medical treatment

explanation.surface: Asks whether an energy therapy could go wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: A sinecure is a paid post needing little or no effort, an easy job.

clue.text: Articles stolen from gala leading to long hiatus

indicators.note: the first piece comes before the second
the articles are taken away from the word gala, leaving what remains

parts.note: a is the indefinite article, so two articles are two As
to itch for something is to long for it

explanation.surface: Items stolen from a festive gala lead to a long pause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stolen from' removes both As from GALA, leaving GL.
explanation.definitionFit: A glitch is a sudden fault or interruption, a hiatus in smooth running.

clue.text: Fruit item, perhaps bit of orange, eaten by the German folk hero

parts.note: a fruit pie is a dish of fruit

indicators.note: the seed is swallowed up inside the German article

parts.note: der is a German word for the
a pip is a seed, for example from an orange

explanation.surface: A pie and an orange pip consumed by a German legendary figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the German' is the German word for 'the', and the definition is just 'folk hero'.
explanation.definitionFit: The rat-catching piper of Hamelin is a legendary figure of German folklore.

clue.text: Loss of oil perhaps from lighter

definitions.meaning: an escape of liquid such as oil from a tanker
a thin strip of wood or paper used to light a fire or pipe

explanation.surface: Oil leaking out of a lighter.
explanation.definitionFit: A spill is both an accidental escape of liquid and a taper used for lighting fires.

clue.text: Permit sound after initial curtailment

indicators.note: the word for sound loses its first letter, cut short at the start

parts.note: a sound argument is tenable, able to be defended

explanation.surface: Granting permission for a sound once its start is cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after initial curtailment' drops the T of TENABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To enable someone is to allow or let them do something.

clue.text: Second male abandoning fervent campaign

parts.note: mo is a short moment, a second

indicators.note: the male pronoun leaves the word for fervent

parts.note: vehement means passionate, fervent
he is the male pronoun

explanation.surface: A man walking out of a passionate campaign after a second.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoning' removes HE from VEHEMENT, leaving VEMENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A movement is an organised campaign for a cause, such as the suffrage movement.

clue.text: Hard to get out of completed channel

indicators.note: the letter for hard is removed from the word for completed

parts.note: through can mean finished, completed
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: It is hard to escape from a finished channel.
explanation.definitionFit: A trough is a long narrow channel or depression, for water or between waves.

clue.text: Shot over very loud broadcast of Verdi

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for over
ff, fortissimo, is the musical marking for very loud

indicators.note: scattered, so the letters of the composer's name are rearranged

explanation.surface: A very loud radio broadcast of Verdi going on and on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' turns VERDI into DRIVE. An off drive is a cricket stroke hit to the off side.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a drive struck to the off side is a type of shot played by the batter.

clue.text: Criticise the consequences of decay?

definitions.meaning: to speak ill of someone, run them down
tooth decay leaves a rotten, unhealthy mouth

explanation.definitionFit: To badmouth is to disparage; read literally the phrase describes what dental rot leaves you with.

clue.text: Underground sign with misplaced name and indicator of time

parts.note: the metro is an underground railway

indicators.note: the letter for name is shifted to another place in the word for sign

parts.note: an omen is a sign of things to come

explanation.surface: An Underground sign with a name put in the wrong place, and a clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misplaced' moves the N of OMEN to the front, giving NOME.
explanation.definitionFit: A metronome ticks out the tempo for a musician, keeping musical time.

clue.text: Cathedral cities half-heartedly welcoming Low Church's embraces

indicators.note: the shortened word takes the other pieces inside it
half of the two-letter heart of the word for cathedral cities is lost

parts.note: a see is a bishop's seat, so sees are cathedral cities
to low is to moo, as cattle do
CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: Cathedral cities, not wholly keen, welcome the Low Church movement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-heartedly' drops one E of SEES to make SES, which holds MOO + CH.
explanation.definitionFit: Smooches are kisses and cuddles, so they are a kind of loving embrace.

clue.text: Biographer's topic, sentence after sentence?

indicators.note: the first sentence word comes after the second one in the answer

parts.note: life is a sentence of life imprisonment
time is a prison sentence, as in doing time

explanation.surface: A biographer writing one sentence after another.
explanation.walkthrough: Both sentences are prison terms, not grammatical sentences.
explanation.definitionFit: A biography covers the whole span of a person's existence from birth to death.

clue.text: Copper infiltrating network, getting a break

indicators.note: the metal symbol gets inside the computer network

parts.note: LAN is a local area network
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A police officer infiltrating a criminal network gets a lucky break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a policeman but is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: A lacuna is a gap or missing portion, a break in a text or sequence.

clue.text: Second group securing right to deliver web content

indicators.note: the second and group hold the abbreviation for right inside them

parts.note: a team is a group working together

explanation.surface: A second team secures the rights to deliver content online.
explanation.definitionFit: To stream is to transmit audio or video over the internet continuously.

clue.text: I will also cut round pieces to get souvenir

indicators.note: the shortened phrase goes round the pieces
the phrase is cut short by losing its last letter

parts.note: me too means I will also
chessmen, chess pieces, are men

explanation.surface: Someone joining in cutting round pieces to make a keepsake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' drops the final O of the phrase meaning 'I will also'; 'pieces' are chessmen.
explanation.definitionFit: A memento is an object kept as a reminder, the same as a souvenir.

clue.text: Rook I let in to visit occupant of bell tower

indicators.note: the visiting phrase opens up to admit the rook and I

parts.note: to call on someone is to visit them
R is the chess notation for rook

explanation.surface: A rook, allowed in, visits a bird living in the bell tower.
explanation.walkthrough: R + I go inside CALL ON after CA.
explanation.definitionFit: A carillon is a set of tuned bells hung in a tower, so it lives in the belfry.

clue.text: True line of kings dismissing pretender finally

indicators.note: the last letter of the pretender is sent away from the regal word

parts.note: royal means of kings

indicators.note: the last letter of pretender is the one taken

explanation.surface: A true royal line throws out a pretender to the throne.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes R from pretender; 'dismissing' removes it from ROYAL, leaving OYAL.
explanation.definitionFit: True in the sense of faithful and steadfast, as a true friend is a devoted one.

clue.text: Very British form of decoration?

indicators.note: very here means saying the word for British twice over, as an intensifier

parts.note: Pom is Australian slang for a British person

explanation.surface: A very British style of ornament.
explanation.walkthrough: Pom is Australian and New Zealand slang for a Briton; doubling it makes it 'very' so.
explanation.definitionFit: A pompom is a woollen ball used to decorate a hat or other garment.

clue.text: Reporters continue to ask questions?

definitions.meaning: to keep urging or questioning someone

explanation.definitionFit: The press means journalists as a body, and to press someone is to keep pushing them with questions.

clue.text: Lots of plans out of time, sadly

indicators.note: the letter for time goes out of the word for a book of plans

parts.note: an atlas is a book full of maps or plans

explanation.surface: Plans running out of time, which is a pity.
explanation.definitionFit: Alas is an exclamation of regret, used where one might say unfortunately.

clue.text: Workman's force in the main requiring some duplication

indicators.note: one letter of the sea force has to be written twice over, duplicated in place

parts.note: the main is the sea, and the navy is the force that serves on it

explanation.surface: A worker's strength at sea needs some doubling.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'Workman's' is 'is', a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A navvy is a labourer digging roads, canals or railways, a manual workman.

clue.text: Time for children to tour neighbourhood — mostly permitted when woman's about

definitions.text: Time for children to tour neighbourhood

indicators.note: the woman goes around the shortened word

parts.note: hen is slang for a woman; the 's stands for is

indicators.note: most of the word is kept, losing its last letter

parts.note: allowed means permitted

explanation.surface: Children touring the neighbourhood are mostly allowed out when a woman is around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the last letter of the word for permitted; hen is informal (chiefly Scottish) for a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: On 31 October children go door to door trick-or-treating around their streets.

clue.text: Ready description of total mechanical failure?

definitions.meaning: prepared to start, as a launch is
read as every system going, packing up, it describes complete breakdown

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase signals everything is ready for launch, but 'go' can also mean break down.
